anomaly_signals.detail: 629 errors out of 1000 spans (62.9% error rate) — acting as the primary funnel for all downstream failures; cascading errors from backend services are surfacing here at an alarming rate.

259 errors out of 1000 spans (25.9% error rate), likely compounded by postgres-auth degradation (124 errors / 1000 spans, 12.4% error rate), suggesting DB-backed auth lookups are failing under the payment_outage scenario.
235 errors out of 476 spans (49.4% error rate) — nearly half of all agent invocations are failing, consistent with downstream tool and LLM failures.
205 genAI tool failures recorded globally; tool-executor itself shows 202 errors out of 464 spans (43.5% error rate), indicating tool invocation reliability is severely degraded.

126 errors out of 395 spans (31.9% error rate), with postgres-payments also degraded (72 errors / 395 spans, 18.2% error rate). Core payment_outage scenario confirmed here — DB-backed payment processing is failing.

116 errors out of 877 spans (13.2% error rate) alongside a system-wide p99 latency of 25,836 ms — LLM calls are a primary latency driver; 29 token truncations further indicate overloaded or misconfigured inference endpoints.
29 token truncation events detected — prompts or responses are being cut short, likely due to context window exhaustion or a max-token misconfiguration under load.
82 errors out of 476 spans (17.2% error rate) — memory retrieval is unreliable, degrading agent reasoning quality for all affected traces.
65 errors out of 238 spans (27.3% error rate) — orchestration layer is failing to complete workflows, likely due to cascading failures from payments-service and agent-service.

recommended_action: Immediately investigate and restore payments-service and postgres-payments — the active payment_outage scenario is the root cause cascading errors through api-gateway (62.9% error rate), agent-service (49.4%), and tool-executor (43.5%). Simultaneously: (1) circuit-break payment flows at the api-gateway to prevent further cascade; (2) check postgres-payments connection pool and replica health; (3) review llm-gemini timeout and token-limit configuration to address the 29 truncations and high p99 latency (~26s); (4) triage tool-executor failure modes to determine if payment-related tools are the sole failure path.
summary: A confirmed payment_outage scenario is causing widespread cascade failures across the stack, with a 25.28% overall error rate and a critical p99 latency of ~25.8 seconds. The api-gateway is absorbing the highest absolute error volume (629 errors), while payments-service, postgres-payments, agent-service, and tool-executor all show error rates exceeding 30–50%, with additional LLM degradation (116 errors, 29 token truncations) further compounding end-to-end reliability.
